### II.11 (47). c. 1948 – 49 — Birth of William Buckler

Act II: Tenancies · Scene id: ghf-19480101-1 · Date: 1948-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Source pending

William (Billy) Buckler is born at the farm on 25 August 1948 (the date given in the 1987 Court of Appeal judgment).

> What we now know: Mary's son and heir, who defended the house in court and was evicted in 1988.
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

### III.1 (48). 2 February 1949 — The 1949 tenancy

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19490202-1 · Date: 1949-02-02 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

John Williams surrenders his tenancy. Frederick Buckler's yearly tenancy from Western Ground Rents begins on 2 February 1949. It is not put in writing.

> The received account: Frederick became the tenant of the farm, and the family lived in the farmhouse under his tenancy.
> Wording: "the farm" — Used for Frederick's tenancy in every later account.
> What we now know: An unwritten tenancy of the fields, Parcel B. Mary was not a party and rejected any suggestion that the house was in it; she then held the paper title to Parcel A. Describing it as a tenancy of "the farm" was the first attempt to make her occupation of her own house look permissive.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 1 to make Mary look permitted: her house spoken of as part of Frederick's unwritten fields tenancy (Mary rejects it; she still holds the paper title)
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold: Western Ground Rents · tenant: Frederick Buckler (unwritten, from 1949)

- Court record: Frederick Buckler — the 1949 tenancy — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Wiki page: The Two Parcels — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/the-two-parcels/
- Analysis: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/case-analysis-connections-patterns-questions/

### III.2 (49). June 1950 – c. 1952 — The blanket box

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19500601-1 · Date: 1950-06-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Mary's statement

Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement records that in June 1950 Mr Knapp, a Penarth estate agent, placed a lodger, Bruce Sutherland, at the farmhouse. He stayed about two years, and later told her he had taken "the papers which were in the blanket box including the agreement relating to the farm" and given them to Mr Knapp.

> The received account: If the family ever had documents, they could not produce them.
> Wording: "No such documents were, however, ever produced." — Court of Appeal, 1987.
> What we now know: The papers that proved the family's title, kept in a blanket box, were carried out of the house by a lodger an estate agent had placed under their roof, and handed to that agent. It happened a year after Mary refused a tenancy of the farmhouse and asserted ownership, and within three years of the landlord's first court case; Mary believed the two were connected. For the rest of her life she was told to produce documents that had been taken from her. The title was never extinguished. Only its proof was taken.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Williamses · their deeds taken from the blanket box (missing from now on; title buried, not extinguished)

- Mary's statement: Mary (Nancy) Williams's statement (c. 1974) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams-statement/
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — papers taken — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#papers-taken
- Analysis: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/case-analysis-connections-patterns-questions/
- Analysis: Register Additions — 6 October 2026 (A-080: Mr Knapp) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/master-scrutiny-issue-register/additions-2026-10-06/

### III.3 (50). 1952 – 53 — Last rent on the fields

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19521010-1 · Date: 1952-10-10 · Parcel: Fields (B) · Basis: Court record

On 10 October 1952 the landlord's agents write that they will not proceed with a letting to Frederick. He pays his last rent in 1953.

> The received account: The tenant stopped paying rent on the farm.
> What we now know: Rent stopped on the fields, Parcel B. No rent had been paid on Parcel A since 1928.
- Court record: Frederick Buckler — 1952 letter — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#tenancy-1949
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/

### III.4 (51). 2 February – 4 July 1955 — The 1955 possession order

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19550202-1 · Date: 1955-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Court record

On 2 February 1955 a notice to quit served on Frederick Buckler expires. Western Ground Rents then obtains a High Court order for possession against him, by summary judgment, described as "the whole of the farm". On 4 July 1955 possession is taken of everything except the farmhouse and garden; the 1987 judgment attributes the exception to Mary's recent return from hospital and her strong objection.

> The received account: The landlord recovered the farm in 1955; the family stayed on in the house only through the landlord's forbearance, and from 1955 their occupation was adverse to the landlord.
> Wording: "the whole of the farm" — The order's description, quoted in 1987.
> Wording: adverse possession from 1955 — The clock the courts later counted on the house.
> What we now know: An order against a tenant of the fields can only give back the fields, and that is what was taken. Mary was not a party and was never heard. She had just come home from hospital and stood her ground for her house. Any clock that started in 1955 was a clock on the fields. That the order reached the house was an insinuation, later read as fact. Per the Buckler case, the woodland of Parcel A was taken in 1955 too, passing to a couple in Llandough and later to the Forest of Cardiff. (SOURCE PENDING: not yet recorded on the wiki.)
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · woodland: per the Buckler case, taken in 1955 (SOURCE PENDING: not yet on the wiki)
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 2: High Court order against the fields tenant for "the whole of the farm" (house not taken; Mary never heard)
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents (fields taken 4 July 1955)

- Court record: The 1955 Possession Order — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1955-possession-order/#order
- Court record: The 1955 Possession Order — enforcement — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1955-possession-order/#enforcement
- Analysis: Case Analysis — Connections, Patterns and Questions — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/case-analysis-connections-patterns-questions/
- Archive catalogue: EV-0258 — Glamorgan Archives ACA/2, ACA/3 and ACA/6: Cardiff County Court ordinary actions, plaint and minute books and  — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0258-glamorgan-archives-aca-2-3-6-cardiff-county-court-survival-map/

### III.5 (52). 18 March 1955 — Leckwith Woods leased to the Forestry Commission

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19550318-1 · Date: 1955-03-18 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Newspaper

In March 1955 the Western Mail reports that Cardiff holds a 176-acre Leckwith Woods, bought for a nominal sum in 1942, and leases 106 acres to the Forestry Commission for 999 years. Measured against today's boundaries, that wood lies wholly in Leckwith, about 1.2 km from the farmstead, so it is not Great House Farm land.

> The received account: The forest taken in 1955 was the farm's own woodland.
> Wording: "bought … for a nominal sum in 1942" — How the Western Mail describes Cardiff's acquisition of Leckwith Woods.
> What we now know: The 1955 lease concerns Cardiff's Leckwith Woods, which measures wholly outside Llandough; the woods near the farm are Coed Creigiaidd and Reservoir Wood.
- Newspaper: EV-0259 — Western Mail 1955: Leckwith Woods lease; boundary measurement — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0259-leckwith-woods-1955-cardiff-forestry-commission-lease-and-boundary-measure/

### III.6 (53). 6 May 1958 — The Leckwith Common inquiry

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19580506-1 · Date: 1958-05-06 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Newspaper

At the inquiry into Cardiff's plan to take Leckwith Common for playing fields, Mrs Mary Doreen Buckler of Great House Farm tells the inspector that she does "not oppose the proposal so long as it applied only to playing fields", and that about 130 years ago Lord Bute allowed her family "a slice of land" which is now Leckwith Common. The order is confirmed on 8 September 1958 under the Physical Training and Recreation Act 1937, the playing-fields statute. Her words concern Leckwith Common, not Parcel A.

> The received account: She did not oppose Cardiff's plan.
> Wording: "did not oppose" — Cut short, it reads as consent. The full sentence is conditional: "so long as it applied only to playing fields".
> What we now know: VERIFIED (Western Mail OCR, EV-0035; London Gazette, EV-0287). Her statement was conditional on recreational use, the order was made under the playing-fields statute, and it concerned Leckwith Common, not Parcel A.
- Newspaper: EV-0035 — Western Mail, 7 May 1958, p.7, "City wants common for play-field" (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0035-western-mail-1958-leckwith-common-hearing/
- Official notice: EV-0287 — London Gazette, 31 Oct 1958, p.6652: City of Cardiff (Leckwith Common) Compulsory Purchase Order, 1957, confirmed 8 Sep 1958 (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0287-london-gazette-31-oct-1958-p-6652-the-city-of-cardiff-leckwith-common-compulsory-p/
- Official notice: London Gazette 41537, p.6652 (page PDF) — https://www.thegazette.co.uk/London/issue/41537/page/6652/data.pdf

### III.7 (54). 19 November 1958 — "A Welsh case of Crichel Down"

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19581119-1 · Date: 1958-11-19 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

Mary (Nancy) Williams, as Mrs M. D. Buckler, objects to Glamorgan County Council's planning committee about industrial development beside Tŷ Mawr. The Western Mail reports that land "farmed by her family since 1667" had been "wrongfully appropriated", that "This is a Welsh case of Crichel Down", that "the water was cut off from her house and grounds for nearly 10 years by order of Western Ground Rents", and that "The Glamorgan County Council, Penarth Urban and Cardiff Rural Councils and Western Ground Rents have walked in and taken" (the search text ends there).

> What we now know: The only record of the time so far that the water was cut off: Mrs Buckler's own claim in 1958, as the Western Mail reported it. It names the landlord, Western Ground Rents, not a council. Crichel Down (1954) was the national scandal over farmland the state kept after requisition; a minister resigned over it. "Nearly 10 years" would put the start around 1948–49 (an inference). Per Branwen Buckler (voice testimony, relayed by Sion Buckler, 19 October 2026), the council cut the water over bills it said were unpaid, which Mary (Nancy) Williams insisted had been paid; dairy cattle drowned in the River Ely trying to reach water, a baby daughter had to live elsewhere, and the matter was raised in Parliament. What cuts against that version: the 1958 report names Western Ground Rents, not a council or a water bill; no report of cattle drowning has been found; no Commons or Lords debate or written answer has been found for 1946–92 (committee proceedings and MPs' letters are not searchable this way); and Dŵr Cymru's 2026 replies speak of a disconnection in the 1980s, so there may have been two cut-offs. The article has been read only as search snippets; the full page is still to be obtained.
- Newspaper: Western Mail, 20 November 1958, p.7, "It's a Crichel Down, says woman farmer" (SNIPPET ONLY: read from British Newspaper Archive search text; the page itself not yet seen) — https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/search/results/1950-01-01/1965-12-31?basicsearch=buckler+%22western+ground+rents%22+water&exactsearch=false&retrievecountrycounts=false
- Newspaper: EV-0037 — Western Mail, 20 Nov 1958: "Crichel Down" (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0037-western-mail-1958-crichel-down/
- Archive catalogue: EV-0239 — TNA BD 28/177: verbatim record of the Glamorgan Development Plan inquiry, 19 Nov–11 Dec 1958 (catalogue entry; not yet read; date match only) (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0239-tna-bd-28-177-glamorgan-development-plan-inquiry-verbatim-1958/
- Archive catalogue: EV-0240 — TNA BD 28/133, BD 28/198, HLG 119/3181, HLG 119/3187, MAF 112/1108: files on the Glamorgan (Area No. 2) plan and the Penarth town map (catalogue entries) (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0240-tna-bd-28-133-hlg-119-maf-112-glamorgan-development-plan-files/
- Newspaper: EV-0242 — Western Mail, 9 Oct 1957, p.6: "Mrs. M. D. BUCKLER … Llandough" (SNIPPET ONLY; content unknown) (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0242-western-mail-1957-mrs-m-d-buckler-snippet/
- Testimony: Testimony — Branwen Buckler — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/testimony/branwen-buckler/

### III.8 (55). 1959 — 1959 tenancy offer

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19590101-1 · Date: 1959-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

Western Ground Rents offers Mary a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden. She refuses, stating that the house is hers through her grandfather and that documents prove it.

> The received account: The landlord offered the occupier a tenancy, and she refused it.
> Wording: "the farmhouse and garden" — The landlord's description of what it offered to let.
> What we now know: "The farmhouse and garden" is Parcel A (farmhouse, buildings, yard and garden), less the woodland to the north and the land to the south already taken. The landlord named the house parcel on its own, which shows it knew it was separate. An owner does not need its occupier to accept a tenancy. Third attempt to make her occupation look permissive.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 3: tenancy of her own farmhouse and garden offered to Mary (refused)

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — 1959 refusal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#refusal-1959
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### III.9 (56). 29 March 1961 — The 1961 deed

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19610329-2 · Date: 1961-03-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Deed

Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile Co Ltd and Cardiff City Corporation sign a deed with a plan. The woodland register WA735527 later recites it against land coloured pink, now in the woodland title. The deed and plan have not yet been seen, so what land it touches and what it did are not known. It is not a Buckler family sale.

> The received account: A deed of 1961 is part of how the woodland left the farm.
> Wording: "deed" — Known only from a recital on the woodland register. The deed itself has not been seen.
> What we now know: PENDING (EV-0040). Parties: Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile Co Ltd, Cardiff City Corporation. Land and effect unknown until the deed and plan are read.
- Deed: EV-0040 — Deed with plan between WGR, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City Corporation, 29 March 1961 (recited on WA735527; not yet held) (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0040-1961-wgr-brick-tile-deed/

### III.10 (57). 11 December 1962 — The 1962 possession order

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19621211-1 · Date: 1962-12-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 11 December 1962 Cardiff County Court (Judge Temple Morris QC) orders possession of the farmhouse and garden, with mesne profits from 1955, against Frederick and Mary, in Western Ground Rents' action. The order is not enforced.

> The received account: The court confirmed the landlord's right to the house in 1962, and that order kept the landlord's title alive.
> Wording: "the farmhouse and garden" — Again named on its own.
> Wording: "mesne profits since 1955" — Money for occupation, as if the house had been the landlord's since 1955.
> What we now know: A possession order, not a decision on title. It treated Mary as holding over from a tenancy she was never in. No deed to the house was proved, because Western Ground Rents had none. It was left unenforced, and in 1987 it was used to stop the clock. Fourth attempt.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 4: county court possession order for the farmhouse and garden, treating Mary as holding over (no deed proven; never enforced)

- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#order
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — deeds before registration (29 March 1961 deed) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#deeds-before-registration
- Parliamentary record: EV-0261 — Hansard, 29 January and 5 February 1963 (with 14 November 1946): Western Ground Rents Ltd and ministers: a WGR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0261-hansard-1963-western-ground-rents-ministers/

### III.11 (58). June 1963 — Committal proceedings

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19630601-1 · Date: 1963-06-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

The mesne profits under the 1962 order are partly enforced against Frederick, and committal proceedings follow.

> The received account: A tenant in arrears was pursued for the money.
> What we now know: The money was enforced; possession of the house was not.
- Court record: The 1962 Possession Order — committal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#committal

### III.12 (59). January – March 1965 — 1965 tenancy offer

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19650301-1 · Date: 1965-03-02 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Document

On 2 March 1965 the landlord's agents offer "Mrs Williams" a weekly tenancy of the farmhouse and garden at £2 a week. It is not signed or returned and no rent is paid.

> The received account: Another offer refused by an occupier with no title.
> Wording: "Mrs Williams" — Offered as to a tenant.
> What we now know: The same offer as 1959. The estate's own records treat her occupation as adverse from this date. Fifth attempt. An owner holding a deed would sue on it; Western Ground Rents never did.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 5: weekly tenancy offered to "Mrs Williams" (not signed; her occupation now treated as adverse)

- Wiki page: The 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1962-possession-order/#offer-1965
- Wiki page: Mary (Nancy) Williams — 1965 offer — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/#chronology

A cousin's account states that the eldest son sold "our land parcel" through a solicitor without his parents' knowledge. No document has been found. In 1968 his household leaves the farm.

> What we now know: What was sold, if anything, is unknown.

### III.14 (61). 1967 — Death of Frederick Buckler

Act III: Possession proceedings · Scene id: ghf-19670101-1 · Date: 1967-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Source pending

Frederick Buckler dies, aged 58; his death is registered in the first quarter of 1967 (GRO death index, East Glamorgan 8b 364). Mary takes back the name Williams and remains in the farmhouse.

> The received account: The tenant died; his widow stayed on.
> Wording: "widow" — As though her right in the house came through him.
> What we now know: The only tenant there had ever been, of the fields, died. Mary remained the owner in occupation of Parcel A.
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold and possession: Western Ground Rents

- Wiki page: Frederick Buckler — death — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/frederick-buckler/#death

### IV.1 (62). 15 February 1969 — BP bids for Western Ground Rents

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19690215-1 · Date: 1969-02-15 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Newspaper

British Petroleum makes an agreed bid for the whole of Western Ground Rents Ltd, wanting its "shops, offices, houses in London and South Wales — for their pension fund", after rival bids from Amalgamated Investment & Property and Great Portland Estates. The December 1969 sale of the farm to BP Pension Trust follows.

> What we now know: From 1969 the landlord that brought the 1955 and 1962 actions and the buyer of the farm were in the same group.
- Newspaper: EV-0288 — Press on the 1968–69 takeover contest for Western Ground Rents Ltd (snippets) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0288-snippets-only-press-on-the-1968-69-takeover-battle-for-western-ground-rents-ltd-en/

### IV.2 (63). 31 December 1969 — Conveyance to BP Pension Trust

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19691231-1 · Date: 1969-12-31 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

In February 1969 British Petroleum agrees to buy the whole of Western Ground Rents for its pension fund. On 31 December 1969 Western Ground Rents conveys Parcel B, and an interest in the 1962 order on Parcel A, to BP Pension Trust Ltd. The 1987 judgment calls it a sale of "Great House Farm, including the farmhouse and garden"; no deed to Parcel A has been found. The conveyance is not on the Land Registry files.

> The received account: BP bought Great House Farm. This deed is the root of BP's title.
> Wording: "Great House Farm" — One estate, in one phrase.
> Wording: "root of title" — How BP's later deeds recite it.
> What we now know: By deed, Parcel B passed (Bute, Western Ground Rents, BP). For Parcel A there was no deed to pass; what passed was the 1962 order and the case against Mary. The root deed is now missing.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Held by BP Pension Trust: the 1962 order and the case against Mary (no deed to Parcel A; the 1969 root conveyance now missing)
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Freehold: BP Pension Trust (Bute → WGR → BP, by deed)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances
- Newspaper: EV-0288 — Press snippets, Nov 1968 – Feb 1969: BP buys Western Ground Rents for its pension fund (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0288-snippets-only-press-on-the-1968-69-takeover-battle-for-western-ground-rents-ltd-en/

### IV.3 (64). 1971 — The 1971 abstract of title

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19710101-1 · Date: 1971-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

An abstract of title is prepared for BP Pension Trust. In 2026 HM Land Registry writes that an abstract "dated 1971 was lodged with the application for first registration" of WA231076, and that for WA240304 "we had sight of a copy of a 1971 abstract of title". It is not listed among the surviving records, and its contents are not held.

> What we now know: The 1971 abstract was the paper on which both first registrations rested; HM Land Registry no longer lists it among the surviving file items.
- Official correspondence: HM Land Registry correspondence — letter of 19 April 2026 (M39) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/hm-land-registry-correspondence/#m39

Cwm Cydfin, the wooded valley at Leckwith, is notified as a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI 0524). It is re-notified on 9 December 1985.

### IV.5 (66). 1970 – 72 — Village green and planning permission

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19720725-1 · Date: 1972-07-25 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

On 16 June 1970 land beside Leckwith Road is provisionally registered as village green VG41 (the date stamped on the VG 41 provisional register map). On 25 July 1972 planning permission is granted for housing on the site, while Mary lives in the farmhouse.

> The received account: Ordinary planning of an under-used farm.
> Wording: "the site" — Both parcels treated as one development site.
> What we now know: Permission was granted over a house whose ownership was disputed, while its owner lived in it. In 1990 a condition of the outline permission provided for a 0.25-acre village green beside the site. Per the Buckler case, the land south of the farmhouse, part of Parcel A, was taken by the council and laid out as a green in the 1980s. (SOURCE PENDING: not yet recorded on the wiki.)
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold: the Williamses (Mary in the house) · land beside Leckwith Road provisionally registered as village green VG41 (16 June 1970)

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/
- Legislation: Commons Registration (Glamorgan) Act 1983 (c. ix): validates the registers of common land only; village greens are not covered — https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukla/1983/9
- Legislation: EV-0232 — Commons Registration (Glamorgan) Act 1983: common land registers only (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0232-commons-registration-glamorgan-act-1983/

### IV.6 (67). 31 July 1972 — Village green objections close

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19720731-1 · Date: 1972-07-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Public record

The second objection period under the Commons Registration Act 1965 ends. It covers VG41, the land by Leckwith Road provisionally registered as a village green on 16 June 1970. Notice of the registration is given to the public; no personal notice to the occupiers of the farm is required.

> What we now know: VG41's objection window closed with public notice only; whether the occupiers of the farmhouse ever knew of it is not recorded.
- Public record: EV-0263 — Commons registration 1965: publicity and Glamorgan notices (VG41) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0263-commons-registration-1965-publicity-glamorgan-notices-vg41/

### IV.7 (68). 1974 — Royal Commission survey

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19740101-1 · Date: 1974-01-01 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

H. J. Thomas's 1974 survey and R. F. Suggett's December 1988 note are separate records. The HER entry records that the house remained partially recorded because access was restricted by an ownership dispute. The survey predates demolition on 6 December 1988; Suggett's note postdates it. The evidence currently identified does not establish that listing was legally required, that demolition was unlawful, or what was submitted to the European Commission of Human Rights.

> The received account: A routine, incomplete survey.
> What we now know: A public body recorded in 1974 that the ownership of the house was disputed.
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### IV.8 (69). 15 April 1974 — Open day

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19740415-1 · Date: 1974-04-15 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 15 April 1974 Mary opens the farmhouse to the public. The Daily Telegraph reports her saying ownership has been disputed for 25 years and her solicitors tell her she has a valid case.

> The received account: A campaign to save an old building.
> Wording: "valid claim" — Reported as a claim, not a title.
> What we now know: A woman of sixty, who had lost a leg, opened her home to the nation. Hundreds came. A thousand signed. She told a national newspaper the house was hers. The public stood with Mary. It changed nothing.
- Newspaper: Daily Telegraph, 16 April 1974, 'Open day to save ancient Welsh house' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n03
- Wiki page: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action

### IV.9 (70). 3 July 1974 — 1974 possession action

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19740703-1 · Date: 1974-07-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

BP Pension Trust brings a county court action for possession. On 3 July 1974 the case is part heard and adjourned for a formal defence to be filed; Mary's defence then pleads that the action is barred under the Limitation Act 1939. Her statement describes the 1877 sale. The case is never relisted.

> The received account: An action that went nowhere.
> Wording: "part-heard" — Treated afterwards as if nothing had been decided because nothing needed deciding.
> What we now know: The only time Mary's title to Parcel A was put before a court. It was never decided, and so never extinguished. Her statement set out the two parcels; no lawyer of hers ever built a case on it.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claimed by Mary, in occupation · ownership pleaded in her defence after the 3 July 1974 adjournment (never decided)

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the action — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#action
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/

### IV.10 (71). September – October 1974 — The 1974 letters

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19741031-1 · Date: 1974-10-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 19 September 1974 BP is given leave to enforce the 1962 order; Mary had not been given notice. On 31 October the warrant is withdrawn, and BP writes to "Mary Buckler" (the family copy; the Court of Appeal describes the letters as addressed to Mrs Buckler, "described again as Mrs Williams") that she may remain in the farmhouse under licence. She does not accept.

> The received account: BP kindly let an elderly, ill woman stay in the house rent free.
> Wording: "licence" — BP's letters, as the courts later described them.
> Wording: "because of her ill health" — BP's explanation to the press in 1988.
> What we now know: A woman in a wheelchair, who had lost a leg, was told by an oil company's pension fund that she could stay in her own house under licence. She never asked for it. She never accepted it. It arrived while her claim to own the house stood undecided before the county court. Thirteen years later the Court of Appeal relied on it to give BP possession.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Attempt 6: BP's "licence" letters to Mary, 31 October 1974 (never accepted); 1962 warrant withdrawn

- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#letters
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Court record: The 1974 Licence Letters — the warrant — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1974-licence-letters/#warrant

### IV.11 (72). 19 November, 1970s (year unclear) — Letter to the Western Mail

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19741119-1 · Date: 1974-11-19 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

A letter to the Western Mail, dated 19 November (year unclear), traces the land's descent.

> The received account: A local antiquarian's objection.
> What we now know: The chain of title and the site's importance were in print before the demolition.

### IV.12 (73). 23 May 1975 — The 1975 conveyance

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19750523-1 · Date: 1975-05-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 23 May 1975 BP Pension Trust conveys property at Great House Farm, with a plan, to BP Properties Ltd. The Court of Appeal later calls it "the actual conveyance of the farmhouse and garden".

> The received account: An internal transfer within the BP group.
> Wording: "the actual conveyance of the farmhouse and garden" — Court of Appeal, 1987.
> What we now know: A conveyance of Parcel A between two BP companies, while Mary lived in it and claimed it, with no earlier deed to Parcel A behind it. It shows BP treated the house as a separate parcel. From here the synthetic Parcel A has a deed.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Paper: conveyance BP Pension Trust → BP Properties of "the farmhouse and garden" (no earlier deed to Parcel A behind it)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — conveyances — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#conveyances

### IV.13 (74). 1 December 1975 — Compulsory registration begins

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19751201-1 · Date: 1975-12-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Public record

From 1 December 1975 a sale of land in the Vale of Glamorgan must be registered at HM Land Registry. The 1969 and May 1975 conveyances come before this date; the November 1982 sale of the fields falls after it and is lodged within eleven days. The February 1983 application for the farmhouse was most likely voluntary.

> The received account: Every transfer of the farm had to be registered at once.
> What we now know: Registration became compulsory in the Vale only on 1 December 1975, so the earlier conveyances were not void for want of registration. The Gazette notice series ended about May 1975, so the absence of a 1982–83 notice is not evidence of concealment.
- Public record: EV-0265 — Compulsory registration 1 Dec 1975; solicitor’s certificate; Gazette notices — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0265-hmlr-registration-background-compulsory-1975-r29-certificate/

### IV.14 (75). 22 May 1980 — Hansard

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19800522-1 · Date: 1980-05-22 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Parliament

On 22 May 1980 Ted Rowlands MP tells the House of Commons that Western Ground Rents, "the most rapacious ground landlord" in South Wales, has been bought by the BP pension fund.

> What we now know: Western Ground Rents, which brought the 1955 and 1962 actions, and BP, which relied on them, were by 1980 the same group.
- Newspaper: Hansard, 22 May 1980 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n16

### IV.15 (76). 7 February 1981 — Ground rents sold

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19810207-1 · Date: 1981-02-07 · Parcel: n/a · Basis: Newspaper

BP Pension Trust sells its residential freehold ground rents in South Wales to Cefn Estates.

> What we now know: BP Pension Trust kept the Great House Farm land when it sold its South Wales ground rents in 1981.

On 1 October 1982 GGAT advises the planners that occupation may continue in the area and asks for investigation before development.

> The received account: Routine archaeological advice.
> What we now know: The warning that came true in 1994.

### IV.17 (78). 19 – 30 November 1982 — First registration

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19821119-1 · Date: 1982-11-19 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 30 November 1982 Linklaters & Paines apply to register BP Properties as owner of the land, title WA231076. Mary is living in the farmhouse.

> The received account: BP registered the land it owned.
> Wording: "registered proprietor" — The status the courts later relied on.
> What we now know: Nothing on the file shows the occupier being asked what she claimed.
> Title move — Parcel B: the fields: Registered: BP Properties, main title WA231076 (applied 30 November 1982)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### IV.18 (79). 23 February 1983 — Farmhouse title

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19830223-1 · Date: 1983-02-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 23 February 1983 BP's solicitors apply to register the farmhouse and garden as a separate title, WA240304, on the 1975 conveyance, certifying they know of no question or doubt affecting the title.

> The received account: A routine second registration.
> Wording: "no question or doubt" — The solicitors' certificate.
> What we now know: The synthetic Parcel A became a registered title. The certificate was given while the owner who had pleaded ownership in 1974 lived in the house. The Land Registry now held the fields and the house as two titles: it knew they were two.
> Title move — Synthetic Parcel A: Paper: registered as a separate title, WA240304, on the 1975 conveyance ("no question or doubt")

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### IV.19 (80). 26 March 1983 — Death of Mary (Nancy) Williams

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19830326-1 · Date: 1983-03-26 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Source pending

Mary (Nancy) Williams dies in the farmhouse on 26 March 1983. Her son William inherits her estate.

> The received account: The licensee died and the licence ended.
> Wording: "licensee" — How BP would describe her.
> What we now know: She died in the house she was born in, aged sixty-nine, still saying it was hers. She never signed a tenancy, never accepted a licence, and was never once heard on whether the house was her own.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim passes to Billy Buckler, in occupation · never decided, never extinguished

- Wiki page: Mary (Nancy) Williams — death — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/mary-williams/#death
- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19830408-1 · Date: 1983-04-08 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 8 and 12 April and 12 May 1983 Linklaters and the Land Registry exchange letters on the farmhouse file, including form D23.

> The received account: Routine registration correspondence.
> What we now know: What the Registry asked about the occupiers, and what it was told, is in these letters. The family have asked for them.
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — first registration — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### IV.21 (82). 26 October 1983 — Conservation reports

Act IV: BP · Scene id: ghf-19831026-1 · Date: 1983-10-26 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The South Wales Echo reports that the Community Council and the Vale planners have Great House Farm in view in their conservation reports as a notable building. No listing or decision follows.

> What we now know: The house was named as a notable building in 1983, five years before the listing decision of December 1988.

### V.1 (83). 1984 — The writ

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19840522-1 · Date: 1984-05-22 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 22 May 1984 BP Properties issues a writ for possession of Great House Farm and adjoining land against William Buckler. The defence relies on adverse possession from 1955.

> The received account: BP, the owner, sued to recover its land from a squatter.
> Wording: "Great House Farm and adjoining land" — The writ's description.
> Wording: "adverse possession" — The only defence argued.
> What we now know: The house was wrapped back into "the farm" a year after BP registered it separately. BP asked for possession, not a declaration of ownership. The defence fought on BP's map: adverse possession of a synthetic farm whose real owner's title was to Parcel B only, with the clock counted from 1955, when the family's title to Parcel A dated from 1928 and by possession from 1940. In the same year the library copy of the 1877 deed was reported missing.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — the writ — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#writ
- Wiki page: The 1877 Agreement — library copy missing — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/1877-agreement/#library-1984
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration

### V.2 (84). 10 – 24 July 1986 — High Court hearing and judgment

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19860710-1 · Date: 1986-07-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 10 July 1986 the case is heard before Mr Justice Hollis in the High Court at Cardiff. On 24 July 1986 he gives judgment for BP, holding that the 1974 letters gave Mary a licence.

> The received account: The court found that BP owned the house and the family were there by BP's permission.
> Wording: "licence" — The finding.
> What we now know: The court decided possession. The question of who owned Parcel A was not put to it, and the 1877, 1928 and 1939 documents were not before it.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — High Court — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#high-court
- Analysis: BP v Buckler: Scope, Decided & Undecided — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/court-judicial-issues/bp-v-buckler-scope-decided-undecided/

### V.3 (85). 1986 – 87 — Royal Commission correspondence

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19860711-1 · Date: 1986-07-11 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

During the trial and appeal, the Royal Commission's correspondence with Mrs Buckler goes missing.

> What we now know: A record of Mary's own account to a public body was lost while the case was live.
- Analysis: Legal Review — the loss pattern — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/#loss-pattern

### V.4 (86). 2 February 1987 — Amalgamation of titles

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19870202-1 · Date: 1987-02-02 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 2 February 1987, while the appeal is pending, an application is made to amalgamate WA240304 (the separately registered farmhouse and garden) into WA231076 (the larger field title). The register then presents the two strands as one corporate holding. The affirmative 'synthetic estate' question is whether a title originating in the Bute-to-WGR field chain was joined to a separately registered house title without the older Cydwin/Cydfin and Williams/Thomas chain being traced through the underlying instruments. The amalgamation records a registration event; its file, the 1877 documents, and the 1938 and 1969 conveyances must be read together to reconstruct the title's provenance.

> The received account: An administrative tidying of the register.
> Wording: "amalgamation" — The register's term.
> What we now know: The registration history shows two separately registered titles before the 1987 amalgamation: a larger field title and a later house title. The affirmative synthetic-estate thesis is that a corporate register view was assembled from separate strands while the older Cydwin/Cydfin and Williams/Thomas provenance remained untraced. The decisive exercise is to compare the first-registration files and the operative 1877, 1938 and 1969 instruments against the plans and schedules. The label 'synthetic' describes this unresolved reconstruction, not a statutory finding.
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": Registered: BP Properties, WA231076 = Parcel B + synthetic Parcel A (farmhouse title folded in, 2 February 1987)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — amalgamation — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#first-registration
- Analysis: 1987 HMLR Amalgamation During Appeal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/procedural-fairness-notice/1987-hmlr-amalgamation-during-appeal/
- Wiki page: Cydfin / Ty Mawr and pre-1877 manorial evidence — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/anomalies-register/llandough-penarth-cydfin-ty-mawr-manorial-evidence/
- Research annex: Cedwyn Estate — title-chain reconstruction — https://bpvsbuckler.bucklerfamily.estate/research/cedwyn-estate-title-chain.html

### V.5 (87). 31 July 1987 — Court of Appeal

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19870731-1 · Date: 1987-07-31 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 31 July 1987 the Court of Appeal (Dillon LJ, Mustill LJ, Sir Edward Eveleigh) dismisses the appeal in BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. It finds adverse possession from 1955, but holds that the 1962 action stopped time and the 1974 letters made the possession permissive.

> The received account: The courts finally settled that BP owned Great House Farm.
> Wording: "the paper title to the farm" — The court's description of BP's position.
> Wording: "No such documents were, however, ever produced." — On Mary's title documents.
> Wording: "since November 1982 they have been the registered proprietors" — The court's recital.
> What we now know: The court decided possession, not ownership. It counted the clock from 1955, from an order about the fields; counted from 1928, it had run out in 1940. BP's paper title was to the fields; for the house it had only a deed between two BP companies, which the court itself called the conveyance of the farmhouse and garden. Mary's documents were not produced because they had been taken from her. The family lost in the High Court, lost on appeal, and were refused by the Lords. Every defeat was on who may live in the house. Nobody ever asked who owned it.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler · never adjudicated, never extinguished (judgment decides possession only)
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076, BP Properties · right to possession upheld (1962 order + 1974 licence)

- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/
- Analysis: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — what it omits — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#omits
- Public record: EV-0267 — Companies House 01379651: the appellant’s solicitors’ service company was “John Loosemore & Co. Services” unti — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0267-john-loosemore-co-loosemores-services-01379651/
- Public record: EV-0274 — Probate calendar 1991: “BUCKLER, William Beverley … of Penarth … died 29 April 1990”, administration granted a — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0274-probate-calendar-1991-william-beverley-buckler/
- Newspaper: EV-0079 — South Wales Echo, 6 May 1987, front page: the dispute between the High Court judgment and the appeal — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0079-south-wales-echo-1987-may/

### V.6 (88). 1987 – 17 December 1987 — Village green extension request

Act V: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler · Scene id: ghf-19871217-1 · Date: 1987-12-17 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Council minutes

Llandough Community Council minutes for 1987 record that there is "no justification" for submitting a right of way from Great House Farm to the Swiss Cottages, and name Debenham Tewson as "the agents for BP Properties". At the meeting of 17 December 1987 a resident's letter asks for VG41 to be "extended up to the farm wall"; the farm roadway is called "an unofficial access route", and the council's Penlan Road licence is recorded as terminated by Debenham Tewson.

> What we now know: In 1987, while the appeal was decided, the council's minutes treated the farm roadway as unofficial and recorded BP Properties' agents ending its licence.
- Council minutes: EV-0214 — Llandough Community Council minutes, 1987 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0214-llandough-community-council-minutes-1987/

On 3 March 1988 the House of Lords refuses leave to appeal. The family are given 28 days to leave.

> The received account: The end of the legal road.
> What we now know: The end of the possession case. Ownership of Parcel A had still never been decided.

### VI.1 (90). 29 April 1988, morning — First eviction attempt

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19880429-1 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 29 April 1988 five bailiffs and about fifteen police arrive. William Buckler blocks the drive with a tractor and secures the house.

> The received account: An occupier resisting a lawful order.
> What we now know: Possession was being enforced over a house whose ownership no court had decided.

### VI.2 (91). 29 April 1988 — The chainsaw

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19880429-2 · Date: 1988-04-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The bailiffs break the gate and doors. William Buckler pushes a running chainsaw through a door. After four hours the bailiffs withdraw. BP tells the press Mary had been allowed to stay rent-free because of ill health.

> The received account: The "chainsaw farmer": a violent squatter.
> Wording: "chainsaw farmer" — The headline.
> Wording: "because of her ill health" — BP's account of 1974.
> What we now know: Billy was a father with his three small children behind a door an axe had just come through. The papers called him the chainsaw farmer. Nobody called the men with the axes anything at all. He was defending his home, on land his family had owned since 1928 and lived on since 1667.
- Newspaper: 'Chainsaw farmer vows to fight on' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n07

On 3 May 1988 William Buckler applies to the European Commission of Human Rights. On 12 May Alun Michael MP asks the Lord Chancellor to review the case.

> What we now know: Both were pending when the house was demolished.

### VI.5 (94). October – November 1988 — BP Pension Fund sells the estate land

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881007-1 · Date: 1988-10-07 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Newspaper

In October 1988 BP Pension Fund sells about 1,300 acres of Welsh land to Intercontinental Land & Development (Cardiff) Ltd for £29,375,400, chosen by open tender. In November the Land Authority for Wales buys sites from Lavernock to Leckwith, including plots at Llandough. The Great House Farm site stays with BP Properties Ltd.

> The received account: The land around the farm was quietly handed to the state.
> Wording: "from Lavernock [to] Leckwith including plots at Llandough" — South Wales Echo, 1 November 1988, on the Land Authority for Wales purchase.
> What we now know: The buyer was a private joint venture chosen by open tender; LAW then bought plots. The farm site itself stayed with BP Properties Ltd. LAW's Board minutes for the period are open at Kew (not yet seen).

### VI.6 (95). 29 – 30 November 1988 — Eviction

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881130-1 · Date: 1988-11-30 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 29–30 November 1988 bailiffs enter the farmhouse. William Buckler is taken to Llandough Hospital. Eight other residents are made homeless.

> The received account: The lawful owner recovered possession.
> Wording: "possession" — What BP was given.
> What we now know: Billy was hurt and taken to hospital. Eight people lost their homes with the family that day. A family that had lived in the house for three hundred and twenty-one years was put out in an afternoon, by an order that never said whose house it was.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler, evicted 29/30 November 1988 · never adjudicated, never extinguished
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076, BP Properties · in possession from 29/30 November 1988

The family's belongings, including Mary's papers and photographs, are left in the house or put in the road.

On 2 December 1988 a High Court judge orders that the farmhouse and its contents must not be touched. BP states it plans to demolish and build homes.

### VI.9 (98). 3 December 1988 — Charges

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881209-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

William Buckler is taken from hospital and charged with assaulting two bailiffs, criminal damage, and wanton or furious driving.

> The received account: The violent squatter was charged.
> What we now know: He was taken from his hospital bed and charged. With Billy in hospital, then in the dock, then bailed away from the site, there was no one left standing between BP and the house. Within three days it was gone.

### VI.10 (99). 3 – 5 December 1988 — Spot-listing

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881203-1 · Date: 1988-12-03 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Official correspondence

Over the weekend of 3–5 December 1988 Cadw considers spot-listing without access to the interior.

> The received account: Cadw gave the house fair consideration.
> What we now know: Cadw had already coded the house just below the bar in July.

### VI.11 (100). 1988 (date not established) — Cadw inspection of the house

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881204-1 · Date: 1988-12-04 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Witness statement

Cadw officers come into the house, carry out a survey and report, and remark on the roof beams being high (witness statement of Branwen, who lived at the farm until 1988, given on 19 October 2026). Cadw confirms in writing that the house was visited and assessed for listing by its inspectors; its two photographs are dated 29 July 1988. A further Cadw visit was announced for the weekend of 3–4 December 1988, and Cadw declined to list on 5 December. Our case: the inspection took place in the days before that refusal; the exact date is source pending.

> The received account: Cadw judged the house from the outside and found nothing worth listing.
> Wording: "the roof beams being high" — What the Cadw officers remarked inside the house, as Branwen recalls (statement of 19 October 2026).
> What we now know: Cadw officers came inside the house and looked at its fabric, roof beams included (witness statement of Branwen, 19 October 2026). Cadw confirms the house was visited and assessed by its inspectors, but holds only two photographs of 29 July 1988: no survey, no notes, no report and no record of the officers. The date of the visit Branwen describes is source pending; our case is that it fell in the days before the 5 December 1988 refusal.
- Witness statement: EV-0255 — Witness statement of Branwen: Cadw inspection of the house, 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0255-witness-statement-branwen-cadw-inspection-1988/
- Official correspondence: Cadw, 21 May 2026: assessed and rejected for listing in the 1988 community survey of Llandough; photographs dated 29 July 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/cadw-welsh-government-correspondence/#m12
- Photograph: Cadw survey photograph of the farmhouse, 29 July 1988 (released 2026, ATISN 27021) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/foi-reply-register/#R37
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 3 December 1988 — inspector to visit the farmhouse 'this weekend' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n08
- Photograph: Roof (loft) beams at Great House Farm — undated photograph, Great House Farm Part 1, no. 080 (Wayback archive): the roof beams referred to — https://wayback.bucklerfamily.estate/images/0000-00-00%20-%20Great%20House%20Farm%20Part%201%20-%20080%20-%20EN%20-%20V0.0.0.00.jpg
- Heritage record: EV-0268 — Cadw 13428, Lower Farmhouse, Rhoose: an early-19th-century Vale farmhouse listed on 12 October 1988 (“Interior — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0268-cadw-13428-lower-farmhouse-rhoose-listed-12-oct-1988/

### VI.12 (101). Monday 5 December 1988 — Final hearing; listing refused

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881205-1 · Date: 1988-12-05 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 5 December 1988 Judge Norman Francis refuses to continue the injunction pending the European Commission. The same day Cadw states the house is not of sufficient merit to list.

> The received account: The house was not worth listing, and the courts had ruled.
> Wording: "not of sufficient architectural merit" — Cadw, 5 December 1988.
> What we now know: On the same day, both doors closed: the court refused to wait for Strasbourg, and Cadw refused to list. Nothing now protected the house, and everyone knew it.
- Newspaper: Western Mail, 6 December 1988 — 'Farmer fails in final eviction hearing' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n10

### VI.13 (102). 6 December 1988, 4am — Demolition

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881206-1 · Date: 1988-12-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

From about 4am on 6 December 1988 the farmhouse and buildings are demolished.

> The received account: An old farmhouse of no special merit was cleared for housing.
> Wording: "Bulldozed before breakfast" — The headline.
> Wording: "suddenly and completely destroyed" — The Royal Commission's archive record (NMR 6048945).
> What we now know: At four in the morning, in the dark, before anyone could stop it. Branwen and her three small children watched their home come down. A thousand people had signed to save it. An MP had asked for the case to be looked at again. Strasbourg had not yet heard it. None of it mattered by breakfast. The house was destroyed before it was ever fully recorded. The title to Parcel A was not destroyed with it.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Billy Buckler · house demolished 6 December 1988 · title never adjudicated, never extinguished

- Newspaper: 'Tears flow as 800 year-old farm house is razed at last' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n11
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-07) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 21 December 1988 (reader's letter on "Bulldozed Before Breakfast") (search extract GHF-E090-N15-12) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VI.14 (103). 7 – 9 December 1988 — Local reaction and bail

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881208-1 · Date: 1988-12-07 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

A Vale of Glamorgan councillor calls the demolition "disgusting". Villagers meet their councillors on 8 December. On 9 December William Buckler is bailed on condition he stays away from the site.

> What we now know: He was barred from the land his family had owned.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 7 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-08) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 9 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-09) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 10 December 1988 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-10) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Wiki page: 1988: Possession and Demolition — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/demolition-1988/
- Newspaper: EV-0111 — South Wales Echo, 21 December 1988, reader’s letter — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0111-echo-readers-letter-bulldozed-report/

### VI.15 (104). December 1988 — Royal Commission in the rubble

Act VI: Eviction and demolition · Scene id: ghf-19881212-1 · Date: 1988-12-12 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

An examination of the rubble, recorded in the heritage record, notes a fireplace jamb and an ogee-stopped beam with torus, and the loss of the carved stone capital kept by the front door.

> The received account: A minor record of a lost farmhouse.
> What we now know: Evidence of a house of quality, recorded only after it was destroyed.
- Heritage record: Historic Environment Record GGAT 02038s (Archwilio) — https://archwilio.org.uk/her/chi3/report/page.php?watprn=GGAT02038s

### VII.1 (105). 20 March 1989 — Site clearance

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19890320-1 · Date: 1989-03-20 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 20 March 1989 lorries clear the site.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 20 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-14) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.2 (106). January – March 1989 — Charges resolved

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19890323-1 · Date: 1989-03-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

In January 1989 one charge is dropped as out of time and William Buckler is barred from within half a mile of the site. On 23 March he pleads guilty to the remaining charges and is freed.

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 23 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-15) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 24 March 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-16) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 6 January 1989 (search extract GHF-E090-N15-13) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-articles-index/

### VII.3 (107). 1989 — Rehousing

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19890325-1 · Date: 1989-03-25 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

The family live with William Buckler's sister in Penarth. He plans to live in a converted bus and reports that about £30,000 of possessions were taken from the site.

> What we now know: The family who had lived in the Great House for three centuries were now planning to live in a bus.
- Newspaper: South Wales Echo, 1989 — 'From farm to a bus' — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence-library/press-archive-transcripts/#n13

### VII.4 (108). 6 April 1989 — Llandough listing survey issued

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19890406-1 · Date: 1989-04-06 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

On 6 April 1989 Cadw issues the list from its 1988 community survey of Llandough: Pound Cottage and the former National School (the church is dated 4 June 1989). Great House had been assessed and rejected in that survey. So when Cadw said on 3–5 December 1988 that it was considering spot-listing, the survey's list was not yet out.

> The received account: The 1988 survey had already been decided and published before the demolition.
> Wording: "assessed and rejected for listing in the 1988 community survey of Llandough" — Cadw, 21 May 2026.
> What we now know: The survey's list bears dates in April 1989, after the demolition. That timing is our reading of the dates, not Cadw's statement. The survey itself looks routine: the whole village, three buildings listed.
- Heritage record: EV-0272 — Cadw 13430/13431/13432: Llandough list issued 6 April 1989 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0272-cadw-1989-llandough-resurvey-list-13430-13431-13432/
- Public record: EV-0264 — TCPA 1971 s.54: deposit with the council and local land charge — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0264-tcpa-1971-s54-listing-deposit-local-land-charge/
- Heritage record: EV-0268 — Cadw 13428 Lower Farmhouse, Rhoose (comparator, 12 Oct 1988) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0268-cadw-13428-lower-farmhouse-rhoose-listed-12-oct-1988/
- Archive catalogue: EV-0271 — TNA BD 34/114: Historic Buildings Council for Wales 1988 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0271-tna-bd-34-114-historic-buildings-council-wales-1988-1989/

### VII.5 (109). 14 April 1989 — European Commission decision

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19890414-1 · Date: 1989-04-14 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Court record

On 14 April 1989 the European Commission of Human Rights declares Buckler v United Kingdom inadmissible.

> The received account: Strasbourg confirmed the eviction was lawful and the property was BP's.
> Wording: "the property belonged to another" — The Commission's reading of the domestic judgments.
> What we now know: Strasbourg relied on the British courts, which had decided possession, not ownership. It never saw a title deed. Another loss, on a question nobody had ever asked.
- Court record: BP Properties Ltd v Buckler — ECHR — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/bp-properties-v-buckler/#echr
- Court record: Buckler v United Kingdom, Commission decision (PDF) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/wp-1790112811838.pdf

### VII.6 (110). October – November 1989 — Outline application

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19891107-1 · Date: 1989-11-07 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

BP applies for outline planning permission for housing (89/01396/OUT, received 8 November 1989). In the same document GGAT advises an archaeological assessment, prices the work at £2,000 and discloses negotiations with BP's agents; it is then commissioned to carry out the assessment. GGAT's 1989 planning report describes the farmhouse as having been listed as a "county treasure"; Cadw states it was never listed.

> The received account: Routine planning with archaeological advice.
> What we now know: The adviser to the council became the developer's contractor on the same site.
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Analysis: Source Conflicts Register — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/records-access-chronology/source-conflicts-register/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.7 (111). 23 February 1990 — Homes bid and a village-green request

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19900223-1 · Date: 1990-02-23 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

On 23 February 1990 the South Wales Echo's front page reports a bid to build homes on the Great House Farm land. Llandough Community Council makes no objection, but asks for the land to be registered as village green.

> The received account: Nobody locally questioned the development.
> Wording: "No objection has been made by Llandough Community Council" — South Wales Echo, 23 February 1990 (snippet).
> What we now know: The council did not object to the housing but wanted a village green. Snippet only; the full page and the council's minutes (free at Glamorgan Archives) are still to be read.
- Newspaper: EV-0273 — South Wales Echo, 23 Feb 1990, p.1 (snippet) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0273-south-wales-echo-23-feb-1990-great-house-farm-homes-bid-village-green/
- Archive catalogue: EV-0266 — Glamorgan Archives P35/11–29: Community Council minutes 1982–2000 — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0266-glamorgan-archives-p35-llandough-community-council-minutes-1982-2000/

### VII.8 (112). February – March 1990 — Outline permission

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19900313-1 · Date: 1990-03-13 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Planning file

On 13 March 1990 outline permission is granted with 18 conditions. The officer's report notes the farm buildings "were unfortunately demolished a little while ago". GGAT's further comments of 8 February 1990 are missing from the file.

> Wording: "unfortunately demolished" — The officer's report.
> What we now know: The Local Plan had required the buildings to be kept. No preservation notice had been served.
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.9 (113). 29 May 1990 — Death of William Buckler

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19900529-1 · Date: 1990-05-29 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Newspaper

William Buckler died on 29 May 1990 at Llandough Hospital. The South Wales Echo of Saturday 2 June 1990 reports that "Billy died suddenly this week", which fits 29 May, and that he "made a detour around Llandough so never had to pass the site of Great House Farm". The 1991 probate calendar lists a "William Beverley Buckler" of Penarth who died on 29 April 1990, with administration granted at Llandaff on 11 July 1991: a probable match, not proven, and the dates conflict.

> What we now know: He was in his forties. He died in the village where he was born, without his home, without ever having had the one question that mattered answered. Mary's claim to the house passed, undecided, to his children.
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Mary's heirs · never adjudicated, never extinguished

- Wiki page: The Williams / Buckler Family — William — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/williams-buckler-family/
- Newspaper: EV-0290 — South Wales Echo, 2 June 1990, p.2: "Billy died suddenly this week" (snippet; wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0290-snippet-only-south-wales-echo-2-jun-1990-p-2-billy-died-suddenly-this-week-he-made/
- Probate record: EV-0274 — Probate calendar 1991: William Beverley Buckler (wiki evidence page) — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0274-probate-calendar-1991-william-beverley-buckler/
- Public record: EV-0274 — Probate calendar 1991: “BUCKLER, William Beverley … of Penarth … died 29 April 1990”, administration granted a — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0274-probate-calendar-1991-william-beverley-buckler/

### VII.10 (114). August – October 1990 — Evaluation trenches

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19900801-1 · Date: 1990-08-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

In August 1990 GGAT digs eight trenches for BP and finds early medieval burials. An area that could not be investigated is marked low potential. In October the council records the condition as met.

> Wording: "low potential" — GGAT's zoning.
> What we now know: The 1994 excavation found burials in the area marked low potential.
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/

- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/

### VII.11 (115). 21 August 1991 — Heritage record entry

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19910821-1 · Date: 1991-08-21 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Heritage record

The regional Historic Environment Record entry for Great House Farm (GGAT02038s) is compiled on 21 August 1991. The Royal Commission's archive record (NMR 6048945) states: "The house and farm buildings were suddenly and completely destroyed by B.P. Properties Ltd. on 6th December 1988 amid considerable local controversy."

On 14 May 1992 Ideal Homes Wales applies for approval of 20 houses (92/00671/RES).

> What we now know: BP had not yet transferred the land to Ideal Homes.

On 27 July 1992 GGAT writes to the council that the 1990 assessment showed significant deposits, including human bone, and urges mitigation. Page 2 is missing from the file.

### VII.15 (119). December 1993 — Transfer to Ideal Homes

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19931203-1 · Date: 1993-12-03 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 3 December 1993 BP transfers the site to Ideal Homes and groundworks begin. On 13 December GGAT asks the council for a breach-of-condition notice. The council accepts the developer's counsel's opinion that the condition is discharged.

> The received account: BP sold its land to a developer.
> Wording: "a difference of opinion" — The council to the MP.
> What we now know: The merged title, including the synthetic Parcel A, passed to a buyer as though it were one parcel.
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076 transferred by BP to Ideal Homes (December 1993); later Persimmon Homes (Wales)

- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.16 (120). March – July 1994 — Cemetery excavation

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19940504-1 · Date: 1994-03-21 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

March–July 1994: the Cotswold Archaeological Trust excavates an early medieval cemetery on the site. Published totals reach 1,026 burials. The Home Office licence lapsed between 21 April and at least 3 May while work continued.

> The received account: A successful rescue excavation.
> Wording: "preservation by record" — The agreed basis of the excavation.
> What we now know: The largest early medieval burial population then recovered in Wales, from ground marked low potential in 1990.
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: GGAT — Forensic Review — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/government-public-authority-involvement/ggat-forensic-review-and-evidence-schedule-v4-0-3/

### VII.17 (121). 28 July 1994 — Finds to the National Museum

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19940728-1 · Date: 1994-07-28 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Museum record

On 28 July 1994 Ideal Homes Wales, as landowner, gives the human remains and finds to the National Museum of Wales (95.56H).

> The received account: The landowner donated the finds.
> Wording: "as landowner" — The basis of the gift.
> What we now know: Ownership of finds follows ownership of land. The finds from Parcel A were given away on the strength of the merged title.
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
- Analysis: Legal Review — Fraud, Land and Human Rights — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/scrutiny-and-accountability/legal-review-fraud-land-human-rights/

### VII.18 (122). 1994 – 96 — Woodland title and houses

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19941110-1 · Date: 1994-11-10 · Parcel: House parcel (A) · Basis: Land Registry record

On 10 November 1994 the woodland passes to the Forest of Cardiff (WA735527). In 1995–96 rights are granted to South Wales Electricity. The houses of Church View Close are built.

> What we now know: The Forest of Cardiff says it bought the woodland in 1994. Per the Buckler case, this woodland, part of Parcel A, had been taken in 1955, and the charity has not used it. (SOURCE PENDING: not yet recorded on the wiki.)
> Title move — Parcel A: the true title: Freehold claim: Mary's heirs · never adjudicated, never extinguished · woodland now registered to the Forest of Cardiff (WA735527) · land to the south a village green
> Title move — Merged title: "Parcel A & B": WA231076 and the house titles carved from it (Church View Close)

- Wiki page: Woodland — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/woodland/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings
- Planning file: Redevelopment and Church View Close — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/redevelopment/
- Newspaper: EV-0276 — Press set, 1994–1996: Ideal Homes (Wales) built “Churchview Close”, Llandough (first buyers by January 1995);  — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0276-churchview-close-llandough-ideal-homes-persimmon-1994-1996/
- Newspaper: EV-0270 — Press set, 1988–1995: BP Pension Fund sold about 1,300 acres of Welsh land to Intercontinental Land & Developm — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0270-bp-pension-fund-1988-sale-intercontinental-law-llandough-press/

### VII.19 (123). 1995 – 1996 — Last dealings on the title

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19950101-1 · Date: 1995-01-01 · Parcel: Whole farm (A + B) · Basis: Land Registry record

Rights are granted to South Wales Electricity, and correspondence with Persimmon follows; these are the last dealings on the registration file.

> What we now know: The registration file ends with the utility rights and the Persimmon correspondence of 1995–96.
- Wiki page: Master Timeline — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/timeline/
- Land Registry record: Land Registry Titles — later dealings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/land-registry-titles/#later-dealings

### VII.20 (124). 16 May 1997 — Western Ground Rents wound up

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-19970516-1 · Date: 1997-05-16 · Parcel: Not Great House Farm land · Basis: Public record

Western Ground Rents Ltd, placed in members' voluntary liquidation with other BP pension companies in 1996, holds its final meeting on 16 May 1997, where the liquidator lays an account of how the companies' property has been disposed of.

> The received account: Western Ground Rents simply faded away.
> Wording: "how … the property of the Companies have been disposed of" — The liquidator's s.94 notice, London Gazette, 18 April 1997.
> What we now know: A solvent group winding-up. The liquidator's account (in the TNA BT 31 files) would show what WGR still held and where it went.
- Public record: EV-0277 — London Gazette 1996–97: WGR creditors notice and final meetings — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/evidence/ev-0277-london-gazette-1996-1997-western-ground-rents-creditors-and-final-meetings/

### VII.21 (125). 2005 — Publication

Act VII: Development · Scene id: ghf-20050101-1 · Date: 2005-01-01 · Parcel: Not yet known · Basis: Archaeological record

The excavation is published in Medieval Archaeology 49 (2005): 1,026 burials, 814 articulated.

> What we now know: The publication does not mention the family or the house's demolition.
- Heritage record: Archaeology and Heritage — https://greathousefarmwiki.wordpress.com/archaeology/
